summary: Clark National Forest tower marked on a 1959 USGS map; a 2016 photo credit is the only later record found. No build date or current state found.

events.note: 1959 USGS topographic map of the Womack area (published 1983) marks a Whitewater Lookout Tower on a high point

evidence.supports: Central US Lookouts page is titled Whitewater (Womac)
Tower is in St. Francois County
Tower is listed under Clark National Forest
Code 35N-8E-34 given on the page, with no label
Photo credited to Bob Frakes and dated January 30, 2016
1959 map marks the Whitewater Lookout Tower on a high point of the Clark National Forest area
evidence.quote: high points are marked by the Whitewater Lookout Tower and Higdon Lookout Tower

evidence.supports: Map text places the area at the crossroads of Ste. Genevieve, St. Francois, Madison and Perry counties
evidence.quote: situated at the crossroads of Ste. Genevieve, St. Francois, Madison, and Perry counties.
Clark National Forest was a National Forest in Missouri established on September 11, 1939

evidence.supports: Combined administratively with Mark Twain National Forest on July 1, 1973
evidence.quote: On July 1, 1973 it was administratively combined with Mark Twain National Forest

evidence.supports: Absorbed by Mark Twain on February 17, 1976
evidence.quote: on February 17, 1976 it was absorbed by Mark Twain.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Central US Lookouts page gives St. Francois County, which the record uses. The Pastmaps map for the Womack area is titled Ste. Genevieve County and its text lists four counties. The record keeps St. Francois County; the coordinates were not checked against county boundaries.

sources.title: 1959 Map of Womack, MO (USGS topographic map, published 1983)

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The Central US page gives only a county, a forest name, a survey code and a 2016 photo credit. No build date, height, status, staffing or access was found. The Missouri Life article returned 403, so it was not read. The 1959 map and the Central US page disagree on name spelling (Womack vs Womac). The county question in resolved_conflicts is unsettled and worth checking on a county map.
